analysis.title: GS US TMT ... Software (MSFT, NOW, FTNT) ..
key_insights: MSFT is up 3% against NDX futures down 105 bps. The author has heard little fundamental push-back overnight because Microsoft's two biggest lines are accelerating: Azure is guided to +49-50% y/y cc in C4Q, and Copilot revenue growth accelerated q/q in C3Q.

MSFT Foundry revenue grew more than 3x y/y, and customers building agentic solutions across multiple models increased 5x. Use cases include automated order taking, inventory maintenance and end-to-end business processes. The author says this execution at the platform layer has been a key part of the MSFT re-rate.

GIR moves to about $30/shr FY29 non-GAAP EPS for MSFT. With MSFT Ignite in mid-November as a near-term catalyst, the author sees room for MSFT to build on its Enterprise AI positioning, though medium-term debates continue on enterprise productivity workflows and full-stack solutions (model, chip, platform).
Investors debate whether MSFT is too crowded to work. The author senses tactical length has picked up but notes the big drawdown in MSFT relative to the S&P 500 into 1H of this year.

NOW is down 20%. The debate is whether it can re-establish its premium valuation as a well-positioned SaaS name in the AI era, or whether the 4Q guide puts it back into show-me-story territory. The stock was up 60%+ since 2Q EPS going into the print, so a slight beat and mixed guide leaves room for bears.

NOW's 4Q cRPO guide decelerates to 18.5% cc. GIR normalizes cRPO closer to 19-19.25% vs the 18.5% y/y exit-rate guide. NOW raised its AI ACV target to $1.7bn, and investors debate whether AI tailwinds plus recent M&A will add to or cannibalize existing revenue.
ServiceNow is including deployment expertise in select large AI deals to get customers into production faster. Supported customers see about 2x faster AI adoption and materially higher consumption.
The NOW chart question is whether the stock can hold the ~$120s level and re-base into CY27, with AI Passport/Control Tower product momentum sustaining high-teens+ organic growth.

FTNT is down 27%. 2H billings are still growing just below 30% y/y, but product revenue growth slowed from +52% in 2Q to +37% in 3Q. The author says the move is a read-through for OKTA, QLYS, CRWD, PANW and RBRK today.

FTNT's multiple had expanded back to peak levels of the last decade on the AI security theme. Markets are now more discerning on normalized growth and incremental AI tailwinds, against tougher y/y comps into 1H27.

GIR view on FTNT: it is a growth cyclical business. Secular tailwinds are positive over multiple quarters, but product cyclicality is likely to weigh on the stock for about 3 quarters, with a modeled trough in product revenue in 2Q26. Longer term, GIR is looking at whether agentic network traffic could benefit the firewall business through higher-throughput box upgrades or attached services like the Fortiguard AI gateway.

earnings_insights: MSFT: Azure guided to +49-50% y/y cc for C4Q (company guidance). Copilot revenue growth accelerated q/q in C3Q (reported). Foundry revenue grew more than 3x y/y (reported). GIR FY29 non-GAAP EPS estimate is about $30/shr.

NOW: slight beat reported, with 4Q cRPO guide decelerating to 18.5% cc (company guidance). GIR normalizes cRPO to 19-19.25% (GIR estimate). AI ACV target raised to $1.7bn (company target). Stock was up 60%+ since 2Q EPS into the print.

FTNT: 2H billings growing just below 30% y/y. Product revenue grew +37% y/y in 3Q (reported) vs +52% in 2Q (reported). GIR models a trough in product revenue in 2Q26 (GIR estimate, as printed in the report).

MSFT: debates over enterprise productivity workflows and full-stack solutions (model, chip, platform), plus crowding.
